subject: geography
title: Plate Boundaries & Hot Spots
welcome_lead: Classify boundaries and explain Hawaiian chain.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on plate boundaries, hot spots and Hawaiian island chain.
final_note: Hot spots stay put while plates drift over.

concepts.def: Plates diverge; new crust forms; Mid-Atlantic Ridge, East African Rift.
Plates converge; subduction creates trenches, arcs; Andes, Japan.
Plates slide past; transform faults; San Andreas.
Two continental plates meet; folds upward; Himalayas (India-Eurasia).
Stationary mantle plume creating volcanic chain as plate moves over.
Oceanic crust dives beneath; creates Benioff zone, deep quakes, volcanoes.

walkthroughs.body_html: Constructive (divergent) ridges produce mild basaltic eruptions; East Pacific Rise spreads at 15 cm/yr. Destructive subduction zones produce most damaging quakes and explosive andesitic volcanoes (Mount St Helens 1980 VEI 5). Conservative boundaries (San Andreas) produce shallow quakes only.

India-Eurasia collision since ~50 Ma uplifted Himalayas. Range still rising ~5 mm/yr as India moves NE at 5 cm/yr. Mount Everest at 8849 m. No subduction (both continental); thick crust prevents volcanic activity but creates great mountain belt.

Pacific Plate moves NW at 7 cm/yr over a stationary hot spot. Big Island (Hawaii) currently above plume, with active Kilauea and Mauna Loa. Older islands progressively NW; Midway Island formed 27 Ma ago. Emperor Seamounts continue chain northward, marking change in plate motion.

mcqs.q: San Andreas Fault is which type of boundary?
options: Conservative
Constructive
Destructive
Collision

mcqs.q: Pacific Plate moves NW at approximately:
options: 7 cm/yr
0.7 cm/yr
70 cm/yr
0.07 cm/yr

mcqs.q: Why are there no volcanoes at conservative plate boundaries?
options: Conservative boundaries involve plates sliding past each other horizontally — no crust is created or destroyed, so there is no subduction to generate magma.
There are volcanoes at conservative boundaries — that's where most of them form.
At constructive boundaries the plates slide past each other sideways.
There are no volcanoes because the boundaries are too cold.

mcqs.q: What drives the movement of tectonic plates?
options: At constructive boundaries the plates slide past each other sideways.
Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
The Earth's rotation makes the plates move.
Convection currents in the mantle combined with slab pull at subduction zones and ridge push at constructive boundaries.

mcqs.q: What happens at a constructive (divergent) plate boundary?
options: At constructive boundaries the plates collide and build mountains.
There are volcanoes at conservative boundaries — that's where most of them form.
Plates move apart, magma rises to fill the gap and solidifies, forming new oceanic crust — for example at the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
At constructive boundaries the plates slide past each other sideways.
